author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1967-10-06 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: The word importunity means brazen impudence.
context_before: When you are learning the art of prayer, persistence is necessary, as told us in the story of the man who – coming at night – said: “Friend, lend me three loaves of bread.” Although his friend replied: “It is late, the door is closed, my children are in bed, and I cannot come down and serve you,” because of the man’s importunity, his friend gave him what he wanted.
context_after: The man repeated and repeated his request, unwilling to take no for an answer. The same is true in the story of the widow. These are all parables told to illustrate prayer.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Secret Of Prayer (1967-10-06).

quote_original: Then I would feel myself back in the living room.
context_before: My old friend, Abdullah, gave me this exercise. Every day I would sit in my living room where I could not see the telephone in the hall. With my eyes closed, I would assume I was in the chair by the phone.
context_after: This I did over and over again, as I discovered the feeling of changing motion. This exercise was very helpful to me. If you try it, you will discover you become very loose with this exercise.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Secret Of Prayer (1967-10-06).
